reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The initial board is materially balanced. Bxd8 captures the undefended d8 rook. The c2 rook creates the need to deal with counterplay after the capture.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: The root probe prefers Bxd8 by 150 cp over Rh3. After ...Nd5, fxe4 superficially retains the nominal gain but the countercheck line scores -91 cp. The actual Bg5 line allows ...exf3 Bxf3 ...Rf2+ and subsequent ...Rxf3, taking the retained gain below 200 cp.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Checked ...Nd5, ...Ne3+ and the rook capture on e2. After ...Bf4, Kf2 guards e2. The final gxf5 is close to the strongest local continuation and the gain survives immediate captures, including ...Nxf5, and the reviewed checks.
reviewNotes.level: Five meaningful solving decisions from the reviewed checking line. Rh3 attacks the bishop, Kg1 answers check, Kf2 protects e2 and gxf5 removes the f-pawn. The optional pawn captures that permit the loss of e2 are not the same full payoff.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed the complete legal game through ply 58 and its actual continuation. Matched the preceding Rxc2 to the exact exercise FEN. Firouzja,Alireza vs Tabatabaei,M, Titled Tue 6th Oct 2026, 2026.10.06, checksummed original archive https://theweekinchess.com/zips/twic1666g.zip.

reviews.reason: After taking the loose c6 bishop, the solver needs the b-pawn advance to relieve a concrete double-rook attack on a3. The chosen four-move defense retains the a3 knight or gains sufficient compensation after further exchanges.
reviews.distinctness: Two defending rooks attack the knight on the a-file while the solver uses a pawn advance and the e7 bishop to hold the diagonal. Kxc6 is a distinct valid capture route in the actual game and also demands deeper coordination.
reviews.solutionVi: …Rxc6 bắt Tượng treo đang chiếu. Khi Xe Trắng lên a2 rồi Xe còn lại đến a1, Mã a3 chịu sức ép trên cột a. Đen đẩy Tốt bằng …b5 rồi …b4. Nếu Trắng chơi Bxb4, …Bxb4 bắt lại và Tượng Đen ở b4 vẫn bảo vệ Mã a3. Trong ván đấu, Đen bắt Tượng c6 bằng Vua.
hintsVi: Trước tiên tìm cách bắt Tượng đang chiếu ở c6. Sau đó xem quân nào của Đen đang bị nhắm tới trên cột a.
Tính hai nước đẩy Tốt b và đường chéo từ Tượng e7 tới Mã a3.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Black begins about one pawn behind and can take the loose bishop on c6 with the rook, king or b-pawn. The rook capture is a strong route that preserves the b-pawn resource.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: The played Kxc6 is comparably strong and remains deep against Ra2, Bd2 or Bc3. The b-pawn capture gives up the very b-pawn resource and scored markedly worse against a-file captures and pressure. Neither is an immediate same-payoff shortcut under strong replies.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Ra2 and Rda1 target the knight on a3. b5 and b4 activate the pawn and the bishop recapture on b4 keeps the knight defended. Even a subsequent Rxa3 Bxa3 Rxa3 keeps the published material margin.
reviewNotes.level: Four solver moves with two concrete preparation moves under escalating a-file pressure. The pawn is exchanged for a bishop with an immediate recapture, and no unequal material concession is needed.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed the complete legal game through ply 69 and its actual continuation. Matched the preceding Bxc6+ to the exact exercise FEN. Qin Kanying vs Karpov, Anatoly, Beijing sim, 1998.05.13, checksummed original archive https://www.pgnmentor.com/players/Karpov.zip.

reviews.reason: Capturing the loose bishop with the king exposes the loose d7 knight to rook pressure. Nf3 attacks the queen with tempo and prepares the coordinated retreat of the other knight. Credible alternatives against the strongest defense also require a deeper exchange.
reviews.distinctness: A king capture followed by a tempo against the queen and a handoff between two knights. The d2 knight moves first so it can recapture on e5 when the endangered d7 knight moves.
reviews.solutionVi: Kxg2 bắt Tượng treo. Sau …Rfd8, Xe Đen nhắm vào Mã d7. Nf3 tấn công Hậu d4 và đưa Mã vào vị trí bắt lại trên e5. Nếu Hậu Đen sang b4, Nde5 rút Mã d7 khỏi cột d. Sau …Bxe5, Nxe5 bắt lại Tượng và giữ lợi thế vật chất.
hintsVi: Sau khi bắt Tượng g2, hãy xem Mã nào chịu sức ép nếu Xe Đen đến d8.
Tìm nước vừa tấn công Hậu d4 vừa chuẩn bị bảo vệ ô e5 cho Mã d7.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The bishop on g2 is loose, and the direct king capture creates the material edge from a modest deficit.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Nxf8 is appreciably weaker and exposes the first-rank rook. In the displayed branch, the simple Nb6 permits ...Rab8 with little remaining advantage. Ng5 and a3 can retain the edge but need longer follow-up; neither is a shorter settled gain.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: After ...Rfd8, Nf3 prevents a plain ...Rxd7 by attacking the queen. If ...Qg4 instead of ...Qb4, the strong tested continuation Nde5 ...Qf5 Qxf5 also requires the tactical exchange. The Bxe5 and Nxe5 branch retains the gain after the immediate recapture.
reviewNotes.level: Four necessary solver decisions along this counterplay branch. The knight for bishop trade is close to equal and prepared by the other knight.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed the complete legal game through ply 30 and its actual continuation. Matched the preceding Qxd4 to the exact exercise FEN. Kramnik,V vs Karpov,Ana, Champions Rapid, 2009.08.23, checksummed original archive https://www.pgnmentor.com/players/Karpov.zip.

reviews.reason: The loose bishop creates the gain, but Black must solve two simultaneous threats. Rc6 protects the knight from the queen, then Be6 blocks a concrete e-file invasion that would otherwise cost material or mate.
reviews.distinctness: A long-range handoff from a queen attack on the b6 knight to a doubled-rook back-rank threat. Blocking with the bishop works because the f-pawn can recapture the rook.
reviews.solutionVi: …Nxb6 bắt Tượng treo. Khi Hậu Trắng đến d4 nhắm vào Mã b6, …Rc6 đưa Xe lên bảo vệ Mã. Sau Rfe2, …Be6 chặn đường tiến của hai Xe Trắng vào e8. Nếu Xe thứ nhất bắt Tượng ở e6, …fxe6 bắt lại Xe. Nếu Xe còn lại bắt Tốt ở e6, Đen vẫn hơn vật chất.
hintsVi: Sau khi bắt Tượng b6, tìm cách bảo vệ Mã nếu Hậu Trắng đến d4.
Khi hai Xe Trắng cùng lên cột e, tính cách chặn đường vào e8 và các nước bắt lại ở e6.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The initial material is essentially balanced. Nxb6 captures a genuinely loose bishop and is the clear material-gaining root.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: The strongest root alternative h6 delays the capture and the reported PV does not achieve the same payoff. After Qd4 Rc6 Rfe2, ignoring the e-file with moves such as ...h6 or ...f6 permits Re8+ and a decisive loss. ...Kf8 is a viable more complicated alternate, not a shortcut.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Rc6 meets the diagonal attack Qd4–c5–b6. Be6 blocks the doubled e-file rooks and is defended by f7. Rxe6 fxe6 and the further legal Rxe6 leave a 400-cp gain from the starting material, over the stated threshold.
reviewNotes.level: Four meaningful moves across two different threats. The f7-pawn recapture wins a rook for a bishop and still retains the gain after White takes the pawn.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed the complete legal game through ply 45 and its actual continuation. Matched the preceding Bxb6 to the exact exercise FEN. Reyes, Romuel vs Fischer, Robert James, Meralco, 1967.??.??, checksummed original archive https://www.pgnmentor.com/players/Fischer.zip.

reviews.reason: A genuinely loose rook on e6 is the stronger of two free rooks. Black can take a white rook on a different line, which makes the knight’s follow-up capture consequential.
reviews.distinctness: Both e-file rooks can be captured by the same knight. The learner must decide which rook to remove based on what the surviving rook can do. The strongest counterplay takes a rook on d1 with a bishop and then attacks the knight from g8. This differs from the current B examples whose initial target is predetermined or whose first move already protects the piece attacked by the countercapture.
reviews.solutionVi: Mã c7 bắt Xe e6. Nếu Tượng Đen bắt Xe ở d1, Mã bắt Tượng ở g7 và tấn công Xe e8. Sau …Rg8, Xe Trắng bắt lại Tượng ở d1. Kể cả khi Đen bắt Mã ở g7, Trắng vẫn giữ lợi thế vật chất.
hintsVi: Mã c7 có thể bắt hai Xe. Nếu bắt ở e8, Xe còn lại có thể làm gì trên cột e?
Nếu Tượng Đen bắt Xe d1, Mã ở e6 có thể bắt quân nào để giữ lợi thế?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White starts down a bishop for two pawns (−130 cp in nominal material). The knight can legally take either rook, and neither rook has an immediate recapture. Choosing e6 leaves the other rook far enough away that the follow-up Nxg7 attacks it and h5; the rook on e6 instead can invade e4 after Nxe8. Quiet non-captures commonly allow Kxc7.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Compared all 43 legal roots and checked every root for immediate mate and mate in two against legal replies. None exists. Nxe8 is a viable motif-based comparison but substantially weaker in the full-budget search (69 cp vs 360 cp). After Nxe8 Bxd1 Nxg7, Rxe4 Rxd1 Rxe3 lets the remaining rook take the e-pawn and exchange into a materially closer position. The local material witness for Nxe8 does not show that the lines are equally strong. After Nxe6 Bxd1, both Nxg7 and Rxd1 recover material, but the focused one-million-node probe preferred Nxg7 (352 cp vs 152 cp), since immediate Rxd1 allows Bxb2.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: The legal captures after Nxe6 are Bxd1, Bxb2 and Nxc5. None takes the moving knight. Bxd1 cancels the first rook gain, and Nxg7 restores +330 cp. Black can attack the knight with Rg8, but Rxd1 Rxg7 exchanges bishop for knight and leaves +340 cp relative to the start. Ne6 is also viable after Rg8. Nxc5 is the only immediate capture after Nxg7 and leaves at least +230 cp. The engine also checked Bh8, Bf6 and Bxb2 after the initial capture; these leave the initial gain in place or permit recovery. No unequal material offer is required.
reviewNotes.level: Two solver moves address one concrete remote countercapture, with a check of the surviving rook rather than a long combination. One solver move alone cannot settle the gain because Bxd1 immediately brings the material change to zero.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed all 69 plies of Fedoseev–Dehtiarov, 1st 3-0 Thu 6th Aug 2026, round 11. The exact exercise follows 26…Rxe6 at ply 52. Fedoseev played 27.Nxe6 and Dehtiarov replied 27…Bxb2. Bxd1 Nxg7 is a teaching continuation. TWIC 1657 archive SHA-256 begins 956d6fcd8214; both players have GM source headers and FIDE IDs.

reviews.reason: The loose bishop lets Black restore material equality and clear the f-file with tempo against the white queen. The follow-up exchange produces the material advantage.
reviews.distinctness: Unlike 2561dc71fff73156, where one bishop forks two rooks, the capture clears a separate rook line onto the queen. The queen retreat allows the bishop to take the single rook it attacks and complete the exchange.
reviews.solutionVi: Tượng f6 bắt Tượng ở b2, mở cột f để Xe Đen tấn công Hậu f5. Trong ván đấu, Trắng đưa Hậu đến g4. Đen bắt Xe a1 bằng Tượng. Sau Rxa1, Đen vẫn hơn vật chất nhờ đổi Tượng lấy Xe.
hintsVi: Tượng f6 có thể bắt quân nào chưa được bảo vệ?
Sau Qg4, hãy tính phần vật chất Đen thu được nếu Trắng bắt lại trên a1.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The bishop on b2 is undefended after 21.Qxf5. Black starts one bishop down (−330 cp by piece count). …Bxb2 restores nominal equality and uncovers the f8 rook against the queen on f5, while the bishop attacks Ra1.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Matched the engine results to all 38 legal roots and replayed each for immediate mate and a settled gain of at least a pawn. Neither existed. …Bc3 similarly uncovers the rook but leaves Bb2 on the board, and 22.Qg4 leaves no secure gain on the next solver move. After …Bxb2 Qg4, quiet knight moves nominally preserve the newly restored material equality, but at 500,000 nodes each of …Nf6, …Nd6, …Nc5 and …Nc3 lost the advantage compared with …Bxa1.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: White cannot take the moving bishop after …Bxb2. The strongest checked queen retreat is Qg4. Taking the rook with …Bxa1 permits Rxa1, an immediate favorable rook-for-bishop exchange, so the 830 cp gross gain drops to a settled 500 cp gain relative to the start (+170 cp absolute). Against Qxf8+, Black can take the queen with Kxf8 or Rxf8, and Qxe4 is answered by …dxe4. Checked other available captures and checks, including Qe6+ and Qxd5+, and the top ranked defences. No other solver offer requires conceding a piece.
reviewNotes.level: Two meaningful solver moves. The first capture restores material equality while creating two threats. The second takes the rook after the queen escapes. The legal recapture completes a favorable exchange without sacrifice.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed the full Assaubayeva–Kramnik game from the checksummed Kramnik PGN Mentor archive (Satty Zhuldyz Blitz, Astana, 2023-04-24, round 4.5). Ply 41 follows 21.Qxf5. The three saved plies and the immediate Rxa1 recapture were played.

reviews.reason: Black wins the loose c3 knight and must account for White’s immediate promotion threat. The sample rook capture removes the passer and retains the gain.
reviews.distinctness: Unlike the promotion-check and promotion-square examples bd0fa6a909eff116 and 4fccf3cadb98c9aa, this line removes the pawn from the seventh rank using a rook that can swing across the rank. The queen cannot profitably take the second knight on c4.
reviews.solutionVi: Hậu d3 bắt Mã ở c3 và rời đường chéo tấn công của Hậu Trắng. Nếu Trắng chơi Nc4, Xe g7 bắt Tốt c7 để ngăn phong cấp. Trong ván đấu, Trắng chơi Rc1 và Đen đáp …Qxe5.
hintsVi: Hậu Đen bắt được quân nào chưa được bảo vệ?
Sau Nc4, hãy kiểm tra Tốt c7. Đen có thể chặn phong cấp bằng nước bắt nào?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The queen on d3 is attacked and can take the undefended c3 knight. Black starts only 80 cp ahead by piece count. Taking the c7 pawn first with …Rxc7 leaves the queen to Qxd3. After the loose-piece capture, the c7 pawn can still promote immediately.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Checked all 52 legal roots, with no immediate mate or settled one-move pawn gain. …Qxf1 is a credible queen exchange but does not produce the same gain in two solver moves: after Rxf1, …Rxc7 allows Bxb6 or axb6 to recover the pawn, and …bxa5 leaves c8=Q, needing a third solver move to answer the promotion. After …Qxc3 Nc4, …Qxc4 loses the queen to Qxc4+. At 500,000 nodes both …Rc8 and …Rxg1+ scored substantially lower than …Rxc7.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: After …Qxc3 the queen cannot be captured directly. The immediate c8 promotion was checked at all four choices, with …Rxc8 retaining the gain. Against Nc4, …Rxc7 takes the passer and cannot be recaptured immediately. Nxb6, Bxb6 and axb6 recover only a pawn, leaving the knight gain (320 cp). In the actual Rc1 line, Black moves the attacked queen with tempo by taking Ne5. Qc4+ Qxc4 Nxc4 is a queen exchange. The checked rook and knight continuations preserve the gain without a solver sacrifice.
reviewNotes.level: Two solver moves, one captures the undefended piece and the other removes the passer. White’s promotion threat makes the follow-up matter, but it is direct enough for B.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed the full Gelfand–Nakamura game from the checksummed Gelfand PGN Mentor archive (World Team Championship, Bursa, 2010-01-09, round 5). Ply 59 follows 30.Qxf1. …Qxc3 was played, followed in the game by Rc1 …Qxe5. Nc4 …Rxc7 is a separate teaching analysis.

reviews.reason: White can take the loose c8 rook while under serious pressure on the kingside. A rook lift then removes a second rook from the queen’s attack and gives White a practical response to the knight check.
reviews.distinctness: The defensive follow-up is a rook lift that both evacuates the attacked square on the queen diagonal and guards g3 against a knight check. This differs from saving an isolated attacked piece, checking to gain tempo, or guarding a pawn promotion square.
reviews.solutionVi: Mã b6 bắt Xe ở c8. Sau …Nf5, Rc3 đưa Xe khỏi đường chéo h6–c1 của Hậu Đen và giữ ô g3. Nếu Đen chiếu bằng …Ng3+, Xe bắt Mã. Sau …hxg3, Hậu Trắng bắt lại ở g3 và giữ lợi thế vật chất.
hintsVi: Xe c8 vừa bắt quân. Có quân Đen nào bảo vệ Xe không?
Sau …Nf5, hãy tính nước chiếu …Ng3+ và kiểm tra đường chéo h6–c1 của Hậu Đen.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White starts 230 cp ahead by material but has an exposed king against the queen, rook and h-pawn. Nxc8 takes the only available full rook at c8, where it has no recapture. White must still handle the black queen’s pressure on c1 and the knight check.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Checked all 39 legal roots, with no immediate mate or settled one-move pawn gain. Rg1 Rc7 and Rf1 Rcf8 are defensive options that let the c8 rook escape or consolidate. In the sample branch, grabbing another pawn with Rxd5 removes the rook guarding c1 and allows …Qxc1+ with a devastating attack. Rc3 and Rb1 both score well after …Nf5, so the saved rook lift is an example rather than a unique answer.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: There is no legal immediate capture of the Nc8 mover. After Nxc8, …Qxc1 can be met by Rxc1, with White taking the queen. The most relevant active replies are …Nh5, …Nf5 and …Rf4. Against …Nf5 the saved Rc3 exits the queen diagonal and covers g3. After …Ng3+, both Kg1 and Rxg3 hxg3 Qxg3 preserve a gain. The latter gives back only 80 cp net and remains optional. On the saved line no capture of the Rc3 mover is legal, and …Rxe2 recovers only a pawn. Against …Rf4, Qg2 keeps the queen safe and the rook lift still supports g3.
reviewNotes.level: Two solver moves in the recorded line. Nxc8 wins the rook, and Rc3 is active short coordination against the countercheck and queen attack. The sample has no sacrifice and White can keep the rook against the checking reply by choosing Kg1.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed the complete Svidler–Kramnik game from the checksummed Kramnik PGN Mentor archive (Levitov Chess 50k, 2022-02-21, round 3.4). Ply 84 follows 42…Rxc8. All three saved plies were played.

reviews.reason: White must capture the undefended checking knight to gain material, then distinguish the positions where a reciprocal rook capture is available from those where Black has moved the e8 rook and the a1 rook must escape.
reviews.distinctness: Pairs check evasion by an unprotected knight capture with a change in a reciprocal queen attack after a quiet rook move. The follow-up saves a different piece from the one that captured. Existing B check evasions cover counterchecks, chasing a queen or moving the capturing piece itself.
reviews.solutionVi: Tốt g2 bắt Mã ở f3 để hóa giải chiếu. Nếu Đen bắt Xe a1 ngay bằng …Qxa1, Trắng có Qxe8+. Khi Đen đưa Xe từ e8 đến c8, phương án đổi Xe này không còn. Ra2 đưa Xe Trắng khỏi đường chéo của Hậu Đen và giữ lợi thế vật chất.
hintsVi: Nước nào vừa hóa giải chiếu vừa bắt được Mã f3?
Sau khi Xe Đen rời e8, Hậu Đen còn tấn công Xe Trắng ở ô nào?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: After the exact source move Nxf3+, gxf3 removes the checking knight without a same-square reply, moving White from +10 cp to +330 cp before counterplay. Black still has a queen attack against a1. The material gain depends on answering the ensuing threat.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All three legal moves checked, with no mate in one or two and no immediately settled pawn gain. Kh3 allows Re3 with approximate equality and Kh1 allows Qxa1+ with a mating attack. Only gxf3 wins material. After Rc8, Re1, Rf1 and Rg1 also save the rook and are valid analysis alternatives. Ra2 has a clear geometric explanation and retained material in focused checks.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Immediate Qxa1 allows Qxe8+, a reciprocal rook exchange. Rc8 removes that exchange and threatens Qxa1. Ra2 removes the rook from the queen diagonal and retains a 320 cp swing, with the strongest checked Qd1 allowing Qd7 and queen counterchecks. Re3 instead allows Rf1. The played Qb2+ Kh3 Re3 is met by Re1 and the eventual Rxe1 Bxe1 exchange in the source. After Ra2, Qxd5 and Qxh4+ are the only immediate captures and Qxd5 or Bxh4 answer them respectively.
reviewNotes.level: The two White moves in the teaching line are a direct capture and a simple evacuation of a different piece. The pawn capture offers no pawn recapture. At the initial frame the stationary rook is en prise but Qxa1 allows immediate recovery of an equal rook. After Ra2 the moved rook is safe. No sacrifice is necessary.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed full Dreev–Short game, FIDE World Cup QF, Hyderabad, 16 October 2002, round 4, from the checksummed PGN Mentor Short archive and its archive-player credential. Ply 88 and preceding Nxf3+ match. The actual line starts gxf3 Qb2+ Kh3, so Rc8 Ra2 is analysis.

reviews.reason: The loose c3 bishop creates a material swing, but Black must also account for the threatened bishop on d3. Capturing on c3 lets the rook either recapture on d3 with check or pin the e3 rook once the d3 bishop captures on e4 with check.
reviews.distinctness: The same Rxc3 geometry occurs in active B exercise 73b99e8ef747e9b0, where the learner calculates a rook exchange on d8 answered by the king. Here the rook that captures creates a rank pin that changes whether the follow-up bishop check is safe. The learner decides the order of two captures while accounting for a passed pawn.
reviews.solutionVi: Xe b3 bắt Tượng c3 trước. Nếu Trắng bắt Tượng d3 bằng Rxd3, Xe Đen bắt lại kèm chiếu. Trong ván đấu, Trắng đẩy Tốt thông bằng a5. Đen chơi …Bxe4+ để đưa Tượng khỏi ô d3 và bắt thêm Tốt. Xe c3 ghim Xe e3 vào Vua f3, còn Mã f6 bảo vệ Tượng e4.
hintsVi: Đen có thể bắt Tượng nào mà Trắng không thể bắt lại ngay trên ô đó?
Sau a5, hãy tìm nước bắt Tốt kèm chiếu. Xe c3 và Mã f6 ngăn những nước bắt lại nào?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The b3 rook safely takes the undefended c3 bishop and reverses a 180 cp starting deficit. It now guards the attacked bishop on d3. After Bxe4+, the rook on c3 pins the white rook on e3 and the f6 knight guards e4 against the king. Without first taking on c3, the same Bxe4+ is met by Rxe4.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 31 legal roots were compared. Legal replay found no immediate mate, mate in two, or immediately settled material gain even at a pawn threshold. Nxe4 permits Rxd3 and the tested Nxc3 Re3 leaves Black worse. The immediate Bxe4+ permits Rxe4 Rxc3+ Re3 and also leaves Black worse. At 1M nodes after Rxc3 a5, Bxe4+ was clearly ahead of delaying moves Kf8 and g5. Moving the rook immediately with Rc7 allows Rxd3.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: After Rxc3, White has 15 legal replies. The sole capture Rxd3 temporarily erases the nominal gain, but Rxd3+ takes the rook with check. Focused 1M-node analysis ranked a5 strongest and confirmed Bxe4+ against the passed pawn push, as also against Rb2 and Ra1. Kg3 and Ke2 are the only legal replies to Bxe4+, both preserving the 430 cp material swing. Rc7 and Ra7 in the bounded continuations contain the passed pawn.
reviewNotes.level: Two Black moves coordinate rook, bishop and knight. The rook on c3 cannot be captured. White can take the stationary d3 bishop but concedes a rook to Rxd3+, so this declined capture is favorable to Black. There is no legal capture of the moved bishop on e4, and no pawn offer in the saved line. The passed pawn makes spending a tempo meaningful, while the follow-up immediately secures the material swing.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed complete Palit–Short, Commonwealth Championship, Mumbai, 21 November 2006, round 2, from the checksummed PGN Mentor Short archive with its archive-player master credential. Exact ply 61 follows Bxc3. All three moves Rxc3 a5 Bxe4+ occur in the archived game.

reviews.reason: Black can take either of two undefended rooks. Starting with the pawn capture leaves the knight ready to take the second rook after White countercaptures on a third square.
reviews.distinctness: Active 38ba4006fbbeee0f also uses a three-square sequence, but the same black rook changes targets only after White’s capture. Here two separate black attackers can each take an undefended white rook at the start, and the capture order determines whether White can save a rook on c6.
reviews.solutionVi: Tốt d6 bắt Xe ở c5. Nếu Trắng đáp Nxa3, Mã f2 bắt Xe d1. Đen bắt được hai Xe và mất một Xe. Trong ván đấu, Trắng chọn Rf1, và Đen đưa Xe a3 đến a2.
hintsVi: Hai Xe Trắng ở c5 và d1 có quân nào bảo vệ không?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Black starts virtually even (a 10 cp bishop-versus-knight difference). Rxg4 captures the loose bishop, and Kxe4 takes a pawn on another square. reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Compared all 26 legal starts and checked every start for immediate mate and mate in two. None exists. After Rxg4 Kxe4, the one-million-node focused probe prefers Rf1 (467 cp) over Ng2 (446 cp), though Ng2 is also strong. Immediate Rxf4+ allows Kxf4 and drops the focused score to −524 cp for Black. reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: After Rxg4 no move captures the moving rook. White can take the stationary e4 pawn, or try Rxe1. Rxe1 Rxe1+ gains the exchange and leaves a +510 cp change. White’s quiet Kd4 and Kd2 also received engine replies. After Rf1, Rxe1 is the sole legal capture, met by Rxe1+ to win the exchange. With Rc3, both Rgxf4+ and Rfxf4+ are supported and achieve +330 cp. The final check only allows Ke3, with no immediate capture. The e4 pawn was already capturable by the king before the initial capture, and the sample recovers the pawn value at f4. No new unequal offer is required.
reviewNotes.level: Three solver moves demonstrate capture, support, and a safe second capture in response to a realistic king countercapture. A shorter line can secure less material. reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 39 legal starts were compared, with no mate in one or two and no immediately settled gain of even a pawn. Nxd1 is a thematic alternative.
